chunks: And by this chain, he said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

What is the least of what would suffice me, from the Praise? He (peace be upon him) said: You should say, The Praise is for Allah Who is Exalted, so Subdues, and the Praise is for Allah Who is King, so is Able, and the Praise is for Allah Who is within, so is Knowing, and the Praise is for Allah Who Causes the living to die and Revives the dead, and He is Able upon everything.

key_terms.بَطَنَ فَخَبَرَ: Within, so is Knowing (referring to omniscience)
key_terms.عَلَا فَقَهَرَ: Exalted, so Subdues (referring to divine transcendence and dominance)
key_terms.مَلَكَ فَقَدَرَ: King, so is Able (referring to sovereignty and power)

ai.seo_question: What is the shortest recommended form of praising Allah in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the minimum sufficient praise (*tahmid*) by linking divine attributes to their cosmic effects: transcendence over creation, absolute sovereignty, omniscience of the unseen, and mastery over life and death. This formulation reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawhid* al-af'al* (Oneness of Actions), where praise is rooted in recognizing Allah's direct agency in all existential states. The structure mirrors the Quranic style of *hamd* that combines theological affirmation with experiential reality, serving as a concise liturgical summary for daily devotion.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘

What is the least of what would suffice me, from the Praise?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying, 
‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who is Exalted, so Subdues, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who is King, so is Able, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who is within, so is Knowing, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Causes the living to die and Revives the dead, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Able upon everything’.
en.sarwar: 7. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The least for thanksgiving is to say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah who is High, so all things are subdued before Him, all praise belongs to Allah who owns all things, so He provides sustenance to all of them, all praise belongs to Allah who is inside, so He has the news of all things, all praise belongs to Allah who causes the living to die, gives life to the dead and has power over all things.’”
